title: Variables
summary: Variables are named memory references used to store values such as numbers, text, or objects. They act as identifiers that allow programs to reuse and manipulate data. A variable always has a name, a value, and a data type, which determines what kind of data it can hold.
sample_question: What is a variable, and how does its data type affect how it behaves in a program?

title: Data Types
summary: Data types specify the kind of values a variable can store, such as integers, floating-point numbers, strings, booleans, or complex custom structures. Strong typing helps prevent logical errors by enforcing how values can interact.
sample_question: Why are data types important, and what problems can occur if a program mixes incompatible data types?

title: Conditionals
summary: Conditionals allow a program to make decisions by executing different blocks of code depending on whether a condition is true or false. They include if, else-if, and else statements, enabling branching logic.
sample_question: How does an 'if-else' statement help control the flow of a program? Give an example.

title: Loops
summary: Loops are used to repeat code multiple times. A 'for' loop is ideal when the number of iterations is known in advance, while a 'while' loop continues running until a condition becomes false. Loops help automate repetitive tasks efficiently.
sample_question: Explain the difference between a for loop and a while loop. When would you prefer one over the other?

title: Functions
summary: Functions are reusable blocks of code designed to perform specific tasks. They improve organization, avoid duplication, and enable modular programming. A function can accept inputs (parameters) and return outputs.
sample_question: Why are functions useful in programming, and how do parameters improve flexibility?

title: Object-Oriented Programming
summary: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) organizes code into objects that contain data (attributes) and behaviors (methods). Key concepts include classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, and encapsulation. OOP enables modular, extensible, and scalable software.
sample_question: What are classes and objects? How does OOP help in building larger and more maintainable applications?
